entryAnswer.explanation:
Imports: `readAppendLogPage` and the `AppendLogStorageTier` type are both re-exported from the published `@graphrefly/ts/storage` entrypoint (packages/ts/src/storage/index.ts:1-15), so no source-relative or invented module is used. The helper signature is `readAppendLogPage<T>(log: AppendLogStorageTier<T>, opts?: AppendLogReadOptions): Promise<AppendLogPage<T>>` (packages/ts/src/storage/append-log.ts:160-175), and `AppendLogReadOptions` carries `after?: number` and `limit?: number` (append-log.ts:13-18). The returned page exposes `entries`, `nextAfter` and `done` (append-log.ts:20-25), and each entry exposes `key`, `seq` and `value` (append-log.ts:6-11).

Why this satisfies the contract: the function accepts the caller-owned handle and the two numbers, calls the existing public paging helper exactly once, and returns a Promise of `{rows,nextAfter,done}`. Rows are built from `entry.key`, `entry.seq`, `entry.value.id` and `entry.value.amount`, so key and sequence come from the record itself, never from array offsets. `nextAfter` and `done` are passed through unchanged, preserving the helper's continuation cursor and exhaustion indicator. Nothing is written, truncated, replayed into a Graph, or replaced: no `append`, `truncateAfter`, `size`, `read` or storage-construction call appears, and the handle is used only as an argument. Zero-valued `seq` and `amount` survive because they are copied by value, not tested for truthiness.

Required cases. (1) Empty initial read with `after=-1`: `validateReadOptions` defaults `after` to -1 and accepts any safe integer >= -1 (append-log.ts:95-101); the helper reads `pageLimit + 1` entries (append-log.ts:166), gets none, so `visible` is empty, `last` is undefined, `nextAfter` falls back to `after` (-1) and `done` is `entries.length <= pageLimit` = true (append-log.ts:167-173). The result is `{rows: [], nextAfter: -1, done: true}`. (2) One entry with `seq=0` and `amount=0`: the record is returned as a row with `sequence: 0` and `amount: 0`; `nextAfter` is `last.seq` = 0 (append-log.ts:171), and `done` is true because only one entry was read. (3) A page exactly equal to `limit` with no further entry: the helper requests `limit + 1` (append-log.ts:166) and receives exactly `limit`, so `entries.length <= pageLimit` is true and `done` is true (append-log.ts:172); `nextAfter` is the last visible record's `seq` (append-log.ts:171). (4) `done` and later appends: `done` is computed only from the current read's lookahead (append-log.ts:166-172), so it is a snapshot, not a permanent end-of-log flag. A later `append` can add a record with a higher sequence; a subsequent call with the returned `nextAfter` will then see it and may report `done: false`. Ordering and continuation derive from `seq` values filtered by `seq > after` and sorted ascending (append-log.ts:127-131), not from array positions.
